reply_text:
I found three forward-looking statements by Mustafa Suleyman from 2016, all with "decades" timeframes. All three come from news reports quoting him, not from his own posts or transcripts.

1. **5 December 2016, TechCrunch Disrupt London (on stage with Jordan Crook).** He said general AI is still decades away. Two outlets printed this differently:
   - Techworld: "I think when we say that [general artificial intelligence] is 20 years out, or decades away, what we are saying is that it is so far out that we can't really measure it." The square brackets are Techworld's.
   - TechCrunch (published 5 December 2016): "when we say it's 20 years out or decades way, we say that it so far out, we can't really measure it." The typos are as printed.

   These are the same remark, so I've given them one candidate entry and put the TechCrunch wording in its summary. The text I got from the Techworld page didn't show a publication date. I dated its quote by the event, since Techworld says it was spoken at Disrupt London.
2. **Same talk, reported by Techworld.** On DeepMind's ethics board he said: "We're decades and decades away from the kind of risks that the board initially envisaged."
3. **10 October 2016, O'Reilly conference in San Francisco, reported by Fortune.** Fortune quotes only a fragment: AI is "many decades away from encountering that sort of labor replacement at scale." O'Reilly's own page for this talk (Next:Economy 2016) has only a video and no transcript, so I couldn't check the wording against a recording.

Nothing else turned up. The other 2016 material I opened was a TechCrunch interview about the NHS deal, and the only timeframe in it was the length of the contract. Most search results were about his 2024–2026 forecasts, such as the "12 to 18 months" claim about white-collar tasks.
